correctness.rationale: The unique first-global-minimum splitting supplies two independent combinatorial meanders and a sequence of positive first-return excursions, with every level-zero and level-one observation accounted for exactly. The Catalan excursion series, weighted excursion decomposition, positive-meander decomposition and full trivariate formal power series were reconstructed. The rare cell follows from coefficient extraction and reflection. Exhaustive path enumeration and rational series checks reproduce all coefficients through horizon ten. Finite checks are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: Full primary-source comparison separates Pitman--Tang limiting joint occupations from the new exact finite-horizon two-level law. A previously published stronger univariate finite-horizon maximum multiplicity formula of Katzenbeisser--Panny covers the special marginal but does not state the bivariate minimum-and-neighbour count. Their fixed-level occupation formulas cannot be substituted with the random minimum without an additional joint weighted-boundary analysis. Distinct-site and excursion-height works treat different functionals. An unrecognized general spectral or continued-fraction formula is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier unlocated weighted-barrier, kernel, or continued-fraction law might yield the same bivariate series; historical priority has not been independently adjudicated.
The 1990 finite random-walk-statistics literature is stronger for some univariate marginals, so those specializations are credited, not presented as novel.

value.rationale: The pair of counts at the first two random-walk order-statistic levels is a natural and non-degenerate extremal occupation invariant, and the prior one-level marginals do not determine its dependence. The fully explicit three-variable generating function simultaneously computes all finite joint probabilities for every horizon, not an arbitrary slice; it yields a sharp n^(-1/2) rare joint cell absent from the nondegenerate limiting occupation law. The proof identifies the structural excursion factors, enabling concrete finite-horizon calibration without simulation. It neither claims a general theorem for other increments nor mistakes simple correctness for value.
